requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
Reviewed `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]`. It is the only test marked for this requirement that I judged relevant. I did not rely on `site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site`, which is about site reviews.

Obligations covered by that test:
- **Anchor and in-source reference contribute their selection.** A `:impl: src/lib.rs#fn[api]` anchor plus an in-source `{impl}` reference gives exactly one `src/lib.rs` input with item `fn[api]`. Its text contains `helper();`, so the selection is the enclosing function.
- **Deduplication.** The test asserts `roots.len() == 1`. It also asserts that dropping the anchor leaves the mandatory inputs identical, so the in-source reference selects its own enclosing node without an anchor.
- **No outline means whole file.** A plain-text `src/details.txt` with an in-source `{impl}` reference yields item `""` and the full file text.
- **Refining declarations contribute complete text.** A refining requirement with an `{impl}` reference appears with both paragraphs ("Complete refinement." and "Second paragraph.").
- **Helpers are not supplied recursively.** `fn helper` is absent from the `fn[api]` root text.
- **Which requirements count.** Distributed requirements, examples, and a requirement whose only implementation reference sits on a refining declaration are all asserted `!structural`.
- **Anchor alone.** An implementation anchor with no in-source reference is enough to select structural mode.
- **Dependency tracking.** Changing the implementation file makes the stored review stale.

Acknowledged gap:
- **Mixed implementation and test requirements.** The clause "including when the requirement also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors" is not met. The test asserts the opposite: after a `{test}` reference or a `:test:` anchor is added, `structural` is false and `fn[api]` is absent from the inputs.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_with_context]` carries a `{fixme}` on `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs` naming nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51, which is open. Its body describes exactly this gap: implementation roots are omitted from the bundle for mixed requirements, and the tests assert that compromise.

Existing rules:
- Source access, exclusions, errors and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. They are assessed under `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and its related requirements, not here.
- The anchor code has no separate whole-file branch (`anchor.selector()` is shared). I judged a whole-file anchor test unnecessary.

Every real gap I found is acknowledged by the open issue.

text: :::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
